en: Hymn of Praise to the Patriarch of the Southern Mountain, composed by the Tiantai śramaṇa Shi Yunkan.

I prostrate my head before the Master of the Southern Mountain, the Vinaya Master of Ximing. His wisdom is vast and immeasurable; his station is lofty and unfathomable. To those outside [the Sangha], he manifests...

The śrāvakas marvel at his extraordinary marks, while within he darkly cultivates the perfection of a bodhisattva. His fame spreads far and wide throughout the Five Indies, and his fragrance flows abundantly through the ages.
Early on, he himself revealed the secret treasury and composed standard treatises;

his brilliant phrasing is interspersed like pearls and jade, its radiance surpassing all other jewels, while his profound meanings deeply open up rivers and streams, their measure equal to the vast deep ocean. He resolved and clarified the *Caturvarga-vinaya*.

Xiongquan personally experienced the manifest testimony of the various devas. Soon thereafter, his pure faculties having fulfilled their transformative work, he suddenly passed away within the chamber of Tan Gu.

His wondrous benefits were perfected, and he thus took rebirth within the Tuṣita Palace. I regret that I was born during this degenerate age; failing to encounter true compassion, I have transmitted the three practices in a superficial manner.
How could I fathom the subtle words or penetrate the profound intent of the Five Sections? Having already distanced myself from the lotus seat, it is difficult to draw near once more.
With a voice like that of a lion, you longed for the milk of the Dharma with a mind as vast as space; yet you remained confined by the limitations of an infant.

Now, the hour of Zhong has arrived, and the anniversary of your passing is at hand. Incense and flowers are arranged upon the seats, and the basins are filled with water plants and sacrificial offerings.

May these serve as a substitute for the *yue* sacrifice, expressing our deep remembrance and honoring your boundless kindness. We offer this meager tribute of insufficient fragrance, humbly hoping that your compassionate eyes will look down from afar and take notice.
With a devout heart, you descend upon this ritual site at the snap of a finger; your divine power is unfailing, such that you do not leave this precious abode even when taking a single step.
May your wondrous functions be revealed through our sincere devotion; we pray that you will graciously grant us your clear inspection.
With single-minded devotion, we entreat the Great Master Chengzhao, the Founder of the Nanshan School, to descend upon this sacred site and accept our offerings.

When the bright moon shines beautifully across the sky, the lesser stars fade from view; when the Holy Master appears in the world, the wisdom of all others is left speechless. May he continue to propagate the Dharma...
The wind from his elephant-fan widely proclaims the instructions of the coiled dragon script; emperors and kings bow their heads, while devas and humans assist his spiritual power.
Truly a peer of Upāli, he bears the mandate of the Tathāgata.

With single-minded devotion, I prostrate to the Venerable Master of the Southern Mountains, who was born in the capital during the reign of Emperor Wen of the Sui dynasty. (The following sections shall follow this pattern;
the concluding verses are the same as before.
The conditions for beings of one kind in this land of China have ripened; The Great Being has manifested his divided bodies to respond and arrive.
The moon reflects in the clear ripples, its timing never erring; The valley returns the pure resonance, never failing its response.
Master Zhu pointed out the traces of true monks; The Yao clan joyfully embraced the footsteps of the Sage.
Celebrating this auspicious day as coinciding with the Buddha’s birthday, One should know that the wise act as the messengers of the King of Emptiness.
With single-minded devotion, I prostrate before the body of one who left home for the Path at the Riyang Monastery;
though his traces were cast among the gentry as a filial son, his character was as firm as pine and cypress, surpassing that of ordinary children.
At a tender age, he wielded the brush to compose lofty writings; with green hair, he departed from home, weary of this floating world.
I have exhausted my reading of the inner scriptures within a thousand days, and I have thoroughly recited the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra* over the course of two fortnights.
Looking up to this courageous and sharp resolve that has long surpassed the masses, how could it be that I alone am deficient in the pursuit of righteousness during these years?
With single-minded devotion, I prostrate before the sacred altar to seek the precepts, praying in advance for a spiritual response in this present life.
When Śīla sought to receive [the relics], a miraculous response was manifested; Śāriputra first prayed for them to descend, and they settled firmly within the precious casket.
As the seven-day period drew to a close, they fell suddenly and resoundingly toward the distant void.
The golden stem dripping with dew is difficult to compare to their purity; Their momentum may be likened to a shooting star across the Milky Way.
The land of Wu still has a karmic affinity today; every night, auspicious light rises from the stupa.
With single-minded devotion, I pay homage to the one who sought the Vinaya-piṭaka at the capital and listened for it while seeking his studies.
At that time, the Buddha-dharma lamented its own stagnation; With no place to rely upon for the assembly of the Vinaya, I endured hardship to reach the gate of my primary teacher.
Through diligent study, I mastered the meaning of the Golden Mouth’s teachings;
The jeweled scrolls opened clearly as the cloud-palace grew still, And the silk lamp shone through the night in the deep bamboo hall.
The deficiencies of the Vinaya are clarified from this point on; yet I still lament that I have not been able to fully realize it in my heart.
With single-minded devotion, I prostrate at the feet of the one who dwells in the Jutumaṇḍa Aranya, as I take up the brush to compose these notes during his lifetime.
His traces were hidden atop the peak of Zhongnan, where the clouds were deep and the monastery was silent and deserted.
He synthesized the various schools to supplement the present tradition; by investigating and refuting the various masters, he established the definitive meaning.
His three practices are as pure as the autumn moon’s bright radiance; his ten gates of discourse are as brilliant as the dawn’s shimmering rosy clouds.
The ninth-generation descendant’s faith was as difficult to emulate; later generations of masters could only speculate in vain.
With single-minded devotion, he prostrated for ninety days, practicing the *Pratyutpanna Samādhi* with diligent conduct.
The power of the Pratyutpanna Samādhi is profound and vast; The true capacity of the Bodhisattva can be cultivated through myriad realms.
All objects are empty and harmonious, merging with external conditions; With a single mind, one perfectly realizes the cessation of deluded thoughts.
Fragrance wafts through the cloud-chamber as autumn arrives; Sound passes through the forest wind as the night grows clear.
When the samādhi is accomplished, one knows it only by oneself;
the Buddhas of the ten directions stand in the air, single-mindedly prostrating themselves, while the celestial deity of the West illuminates the path and supports one’s body with his hands.
In the silent Flower Palace at the hour of midnight, Within the vast Moon Hall, he still performs his circumambulation.
With the mind focused on the true realm, weariness is instantly forgotten; Though his feet tread upon the empty steps, how could there be any harm?
The Bodhisattva suddenly manifests to receive him personally; Nata, having received the command, follows him unseen.
The Buddha’s tooth relic was offered to the Master from this place; it passed to Wen-gang and now remains in the world.
With single-minded devotion, I prostrate to the one who relies upon the dragons and devas, who lectured on the *Laṅkāvatāra Sūtra* and whose body received the precepts.
The Master dwells beyond the mundane world, idly waving his fly-whisk; A dragon transformed into human form comes to listen to the Dharma.
Frequent exhortations resound like the roar of a bellowing stone; The body of precepts is secretly bestowed with the intent of the life-preserving skin-bag.
In South India, Vile offers ambrosia; In West India, Nadi requests the interpreter.
Such understanding and practice are rarely encountered in this world; both the hidden and the manifest yearn to take refuge in his magnificent virtue.
With single-minded devotion, they prostrate before him at Jingnan Liufu, where he has constructed an altar according to the Dharma at this auspicious time.
The village is called Zunshe (Following Goodness), destined for the sacred soil; the district is named Qingguan (Pure Officials), a pure domain indeed.
Thus, he constructed a spirit altar facing the Azure Garden (the monastery), looking up to model the excellent regulations of the former sage.
Brightly gleaming pearl cauldrons are linked atop the high summit; brilliantly radiant star-spirits are arrayed across two tiers.
Clouds of offerings from the four directions rushed forth in succession; through the power of his merit and realization, Piṇḍola bowed in homage.
With single-minded devotion, he prostrated himself before the one who had accomplished his task and manifested parinirvāṇa, now dwelling in the Tuṣita heaven in his transformed body.
The fragrance of the thorny groves is offered from heaven; In the Tuṣita Palace, wonders await the arrival of the Holy One to fill the seat of succession.
Thus he shall personally attend the Venerable Maitreya, And descending to birth, shall succeed Pūrṇa in his office.
Resplendent banners and streamers sway in the colorful sun, While pure and cool songs and chants resound through the high heavens.

Restraining their deportment, they sit upright and silent; a thousand disciples who have borne the Dharma shed blood and tears as they sincerely repent for myself and all sentient beings throughout the ten directions and the entire dharma-realm.
The wind of ignorance blows upon the source of the mind, causing the waves of deluded consciousness to surge.

The ocean of nature thus undergoes arising and ceasing, leading to drifting and sinking. One wanders through the four modes of birth in an endless cycle; entangled by manifold sufferings, there is no end to them.

Not hearing the True Dharma, how is one any different from the three hundred million followers of Mara? Or, if one is tainted by perverse winds, how is one any different from the faction of the six heretical teachers?
One will forever invite dark obscurity and dwell long in ignorance and delusion; clinging to the objects of the sensory world is like a foolish monkey finding a tree.
The passions of desire compete and rush forward like a wild elephant without a hook; even if one encounters a skilled master, how could one harbor deep faith?

This causes the pearl in one's garment to remain tied in vain, utterly forgetting the mind of awareness, while the treasures in one's home fill them in vain, never able to relieve the calamities of poverty and distress.

For what reason did I happen to leave the household life today? Clad in the water-field robe and receiving the *saṃvara* precepts as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, I have encountered the bequeathed teachings of the Śākyamuni and met with the precious chapters of Zhongnan.
Yet, I am utterly lost on the path of meaning; I have not penetrated the profound depths, and my doubts remain like ice.

While I am bound by a web of ignorance regarding the abyssal depth, I instead rely on the knowledge of one who measures the ocean, falsely trusting in the wisdom of one who carries a mere pitcher, and thus I presume upon and insult those who have attained prior awakening.

They reject the True Vehicle, taking the definitive teachings as mere empty fabrications and regarding the provisional schools as frivolous discourse. The banner of pride stands tall and the net of attachment spreads wide;
they dwell in seclusion committing wrongs, yet refuse to fear the hidden spirits and erase their traces.

When meeting others, they conceal their true nature, seeking only perverse gain to support themselves. Unrighteousness is practiced constantly, and they sit forever without shame—truly acting as thorns within the field of merit.

Faith is like the smoke and clouds that obscure the sun of the Buddha. Lacking cultivation of the contemplative wisdom of the Three Vehicles, the ten classes of transgressions have become deeply hidden.
Such offenses and contradictions are as vast as space; I now lay them bare before the Ten Thousand Virtues and confess them openly before the Four Reliances.
I vow to eliminate future violations and forever sever past errors. May I universally receive the light of wisdom and instantly shed the faults of frost and snow.
Having finished the repentance, with a sincere heart take refuge and pay homage (the following sections are all to be modeled after this).
With a sincere heart, I exhort the Muni to first establish the abbreviated teachings; Śāriputra, with utmost reverence, begs you to speak of them in detail.
I now universally entreat the holy sages and teachers; first, I turn toward the Dharma-realm as vast as motes of dust to extol the Vinaya-piṭaka.
With a sincere heart, I rejoice in all the sons of the Buddha who have first resolved to attain the Way, until they finally ascend to the sublime fruit of the Great Compassionate Honored One.
I now rejoice in all the conditions for transcending the world that have been cultivated, one by one;
I wholeheartedly dedicate them toward the causes previously practiced within the precepts, concentration, and wisdom, or those arising from hearing, reflection, and meditation.
Dedicating [merit] within the *tathatā* dharma-realm, may all beings be universally nourished and partake in eternal bliss;
with a sincere heart I make this vow:
may we together practice the "goose-and-pearl" compassion for the benefit of others, and may we share the resolve to protect the roots of the precepts like grass tied together.
"I vow to maintain the samādhi of the unconditioned nature; May I always traverse the Buddha-way to open up dhyāna and wisdom.
Regarding the statement in the first chapter of the *Zhenwu Lishi* that [the Master] was born in Dantu:

according to his *xingzhuang* (biographical record), the Great Master was raised in Jinghua, which refers to the capital region of Jingzhao Prefecture. To say he was from Changcheng or Dantu likely refers to his ancestral origins.
This is what the school produces; it is not the place of origin. Chapter Eight: Examining the Languages of the Four Quarters according to the *Liji* (Book of Rites).
Each has its respective office: in the east, they are called *ji*; in the south, *xiang*; in the west, *diti* (pronounced *ti*); and in the north, *yi*.

The *Zhouli* (Rites of Zhou) refers to them as *xiangxu*, which means those who communicate the languages of the four quarters. The character *xu* is pronounced with the third tone (*shangsheng*). Now...
To pronounce this with the level tone (ping sheng) is an error. If it were pronounced with the rising tone (shang sheng), it would be inconvenient for the musical cadence.
Now, when addressing those from Western India (Xizhu), one should say *diti*. Furthermore, let us maintain the established tradition; scholars must not fail to understand this.
The Liturgy of Homage and Praise to the Patriarchs of the Southern Mountain (Concluded)
